title: No root of the chromatic polynomial exceeds the vertex count
statement:
Let $G$ be a nonempty finite simple graph on $
u$ vertices, and for a natural number $k$ write $\pi_k(G)$ for the number of proper $k$-colourings of $G$. Suppose $p$ is a real polynomial that agrees with this count at every natural number, in the sense that $p(k) = \pi_k(G)$ for all $k \in  bn$. Then every real root of $p$ is at most $
u$; that is, if $p(x) = 0$ with $x \in  br$, then $x \le 
u$.
hypotheses_covered: G is a finite simple graph
G has at least one vertex (nonempty)
p(k) equals the number of proper k-colourings for every natural number k
x is a real root of p
